text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate by sending HTTP requests and receiving responses. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before using an API, you usually need authentication, such as an API key, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a certain period. Finally, good error handling helps you deal with problems like network failures or invalid responses. By following these practices, you can build reliable applications that communicate smoothly with other services.
